categories.name: Hollis (1905 'The Masai'), Hinde (1901 'The Masai Language'), Johnston (1902) & Hobley (1910, 1922) Historical Maa Corpus

entries.english: Traditional Maasai Salutations (Hinde 1901 p. 29 & Hollis 1905 p. 99): Warriors/Men & Women/Elders
entries.translation: Sopai! — Reply: Epa! (Men/Warriors) | Takwenya! — Reply: Iko! (Women/Elders)
entries.context: Hildegarde Hinde (1901) 'The Masai Language', p. 29 & A. C. Hollis (1905) 'The Masai', p. 99

entries.english: Major Maasai Tribal Divisions, Sub-Districts & Clans (Hollis 1905 pp. 260–264)
entries.translation: Il-Aiser (L-Aiser, clan of the Oloiboni), Il-ukumai (L-ukumai), Il-Mokesen (L-Mokesen), Il-Molelian (L-Molelian), Il-Tarosero (L-Tarosero)
entries.context: A. C. Hollis (1905) 'The Masai: Their Language and Folklore', pp. 260–264

entries.english: Maasai Place-Name Etymologies Recorded by Hildegarde Hinde (1901 p. 36) & Hollis (1905)
entries.translation: En-gare Nyrobi (Nairobi = 'Cold Water'), Ol-doinyo Oibor (Mt. Kilimanjaro/Kenya = 'White Mountain'), En-gare Na-okwa (Naivasha), Ol-doinyo Eburru ('Steaming Mountain')
entries.pronunciation: en-ga-re ny-ro-bi / ol-doi-nyo oi-bor / ol-doi-nyo e-bur-ru
entries.context: Hildegarde Hinde (1901) 'The Masai Language', p. 36 & A. C. Hollis (1905)

entries.translation: Emorata (circumcision), E-unoto (warrior graduation ceremony), Ol-ngesher (elderhood ceremony), En-gipaata (boys' pre-initiation dance)
entries.context: A. C. Hollis (1905) 'The Masai: Their Language and Folklore', pp. 294–302

entries.english: Sacred Pasture Grass Held in Peace, Prayer & Blessing
entries.translation: en-gujit (held in the hand during peace-making and prayer to Eng-ai)
entries.context: A. C. Hollis (1905, p. 289) & C. W. Hobley (1922, p. 305) — Maasai sacred grass symbol

entries.english: The Two Aspects of the Supreme Sky Deity (Hollis 1905 p. 264): The Benevolent Black Cloud & The Fierce Red Sky
entries.translation: Eng-ai Narok (The Black/Benevolent Rain-bringing God) & Eng-ai Nanyokie (The Red Sky)
entries.context: A. C. Hollis (1905) 'The Masai: Their Language and Folklore', p. 264

source: Public Domain Historical Lexicons (Hinde 1901, Johnston 1902, Hollis 1905 & Hobley 1910, 1922)
